implementation_notes: The futures crate supplies the static form (join!/try_join! poll a fixed set of futures and resolve when all have completed) and the dynamic form (FuturesUnordered, buffer_unordered) when the number of partials is not known up front, while tokio::task::JoinSet spawns tasks and yields results as they finish - the completion-order shape a time-out or best-so-far strategy needs. Aggregation state follows Rust's ownership rules: the collector owns the partial vector or map, so there is no shared mutable state to lock; when partials arrive from a broker instead of being spawned futures, the state lives in a HashMap keyed by correlation id owned by a single task or actor.
pitfalls: join!/try_join! are macros with fixed arity, and try_join! short-circuits on the first error and drops the remaining results - a dynamic set requires JoinSet/FuturesUnordered.
Futures do nothing until polled: collecting them into a Vec without awaiting a combinator aggregates nothing.
JoinSet::join_next yields Err(JoinError) for panics and cancellations - counting those as received partials without a deadline leaves the aggregate waiting forever.
